top_story.headline: FEC presses Sen. Cory Booker's campaign over a $9,178.33 'Unauthorized transaction'
top_story.dek: The agency says the amended year-end report shows an apparent unauthorized disbursement of committee funds and has asked for more information.
paragraphs: The Federal Election Commission sent Cory Booker for Senate, the committee of Sen. Cory A. Booker (D-NJ), a request for additional information dated October 21, 2026. It concerns the committee's amended Year-End 2025 report (10/01/2025 - 12/31/2025), received July 1, 2026. Schedule B supporting Line 21 discloses a disbursement described as 'Unauthorized transaction' totaling $9,178.33, which the letter says 'appears to be related to an apparent unauthorized disbursement of Committee funds.'

The letter says the Commission 'notes your explanation of the unauthorized activity' and asks the committee to provide any additional information as it becomes available. It adds that the Commission may still take further legal action over what it calls apparent improper use of committee funds, citing 11 CFR §§ 102.9, 102.15 and 104.3. The letter text does not say who made the transaction or what the committee's explanation was. The committee's treasurer is Scott Kobler, and the response due date is 11/25/2026.

Other items in today's batch include a 12-page Form 3 from Emmett White with internally inconsistent figures, a $50,250,000 intellectual-property valuation restated by State of Loc Nation for Clement for Senate, and three straight reports showing a negative ending cash balance at Witta for Congress Committee.

sections.headline: Seven sitting lawmakers' committees drew FEC letters or filed with the FEC, plus one termination
paragraphs: Six of today's FEC letters went to committees of sitting members: two about missing or unmatched 48-hour notices, one about general-election money, two about excessive contributions and one about an unauthorized disbursement (the Top Story). Two members also filed Form 99 responses, and one member's committee was approved for termination.

items: Sen. Cory A. Booker (D-NJ) is pressed by the FEC over a $9,178.33 disbursement his committee labeled 'Unauthorized transaction'. The letter calls it an apparent unauthorized disbursement of committee funds and says further legal action is possible. It concerns the amended Year-End 2025 report. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rep. Ben Cline (R-VA) is asked about possibly missing 48-hour notices of last-minute contributions and a $1,000-plus contribution from Eugene Sullivan on 7/18/2026 that is missing from Schedule A. The October Quarterly letter went to Ben Cline for Congress, Inc., whose treasurer is Laura McMenamin. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Rep. Jennifer L. McClellan (D-VA) is asked about possibly missing 48-hour notices of last-minute contributions. The October Quarterly letter went to McClellan for Congress, whose treasurer is Scott M. Hubay. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Rep. Doug LaMalfa (R-CA) is told his committee's general-election contributions still do not appear to have been refunded. The April Quarterly letter to the Doug LaMalfa Committee says the candidate is not seeking office and that refunds were due within 60 days of the announcement. The FEC notes the committee's explanation of corrective action on some of the contributions. Treasurer is Kelly Lawler. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Rep. Lance Gooden (R-TX) is asked about apparently excessive contributions, incomplete donor employer and occupation entries, and a wrong committee ID for the Association of Equipment Manufacturers. The amended July Quarterly letter went to Lance Gooden for Congress Committee, whose treasurer is Robert Phillips III. The FEC says the donor entries read 'blank/blank' and lists the incorrect ID as C30003511. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rep. Shri Thanedar (D-MI) is asked about apparently excessive contributions and donor employer entries such as 'Information Requested/Information Requested' and 'Self/Business'. The July Quarterly letter to Shri for Congress also lists 'New Jersey Brain And Spine/Information Requested' and 'Owl Creek Asset Management/Information Requested'. The candidate is listed as his own treasurer. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rep. Julia Letlow (R-LA) tells the FEC a database error after a compliance-firm switch caused the Column B variance on her July Quarterly report. The Form 99 from Julia Letlow for Louisiana responds to an October 18 request and says amendments filed October 15 to the Pre-Runoff and July Quarterly reports fixed it. Treasurer is Shea Thomas. (Form 99)

Rep. Keith Self (R-TX) tells the FEC a 48-hour report was filed to add a donor who gave through the WinRed earmark conduit. The Form 99 from Self for Congress cites FEC-2034614 and says the PAC on the report was previously reported. (Form 99)
Rep. Christopher C. Collins (R-NY) has his committee's termination approved. Collins for Congress is listed with a termination approval received 10/21. Terminations are not read. (Filing)

sections.headline: 64 RFAIs in all: a few serious problems, a run of template letters, and 33 notices with no itemized text
paragraphs: Today's batch follows the October Quarterly deadline. Six of the 64 letters went to sitting lawmakers and are listed above. Of the other 58, the sharpest are the three consecutive negative cash balances at Witta for Congress Committee, three RFAIs on amended reports at Rolling Sea Action Fund, and nine misattributed Schedule 5-E entries at The Conservative Caucus. Letters are grouped below as candidate committees, PACs and party committees, and notices with no itemized text.

items: FEC tells ALVH for President that its committee name must include the candidate's name. The Statement of Organization letter went to ALVH for President, the committee of Republican presidential candidate Arthur Linwood Van Houten III, who is also its treasurer. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

FEC tells Avila Chevalier and Valdez Victory Fund its July Quarterly is 'not acceptable as filed' and must be resubmitted on FEC Form 3. The fund is listed as a House candidate committee, and its treasurer is Andrew Madras. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Citizens for Melissa Strange is asked to fix a cash balance that does not match its July Quarterly, wrong Column B totals and a coverage gap from 7/1/2026 to 7/15/2026. The October Quarterly letter to the Kentucky Democratic challenger's committee requires an amended report covering the gap. The treasurer is Andrew Strange. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Collins for GA Senate Republican Nominee Fund 2026 is asked to itemize the original donors behind contributions routed through a conduit. The October Quarterly letter says Schedule A shows the conduit but not the underlying earmarked contributions. The treasurer is Benjamin Ottenhoff. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Jenny for Congress is asked about transfers from 'Jenny Victory Fund' that the FEC says appear to come from joint fundraising. The fund is not disclosed as a joint fundraising representative on the Statement of Organization of the South Carolina Republican open-seat candidate. The treasurer is Thomas Datwyler. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Julian for U.S. Senate is asked why an amended July 2025 report cut receipts by $24,331.08. The decrease is on Lines 11(a)(i) and 11(a)(ii) of the amended report received 03/31/2026. The committee is that of South Dakota Democratic challenger Julian Beaudion, who is also its treasurer. Response due 11/24. (RFAI)

Rick for Louisiana is asked why an amended July Quarterly cut receipts by $18,500. The decrease is on Line 11(a)(i) of the report received 10/01/2026. The treasurer, Christel Slaughter, also received the next letter. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Rick for Louisiana is asked why an amended 12-Day Pre-Primary report added $83,320.88 in disbursements. The amended report covering 07/01/2026 - 07/18/2026 was received 10/13/2026, and the letter asks why the activity was not on the original. Same treasurer, Christel Slaughter. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Vote VDO Victor D Orlando is asked why its July Quarterly opening cash does not match its April Quarterly closing balance, and for missing conduit details. The letter concerns the report received 07/23/2026 from the New Hampshire Republican challenger's committee. The treasurer is Victor Orlando. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Witta for Congress Committee is told its April Quarterly shows a negative ending cash balance of $36,546.27. The FEC also objects to the committee's own name used as payee and to incomplete Schedule D creditor information. This is the first of three letters in one day to the Colorado candidate's committee, whose treasurer is Natalija Baranenka. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Witta for Congress Committee is told its July Quarterly shows a negative ending cash balance of $58,959.33. The letter repeats the payee-name and Schedule D problems from the April report. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

Witta for Congress Committee is told its October Quarterly shows a negative ending cash balance of $47,148.76 and loans listing the committee itself as source. The letter lists loans of $350.00, $3,063.74, $19,426.71, $80,000.00 and -$52.00 on 7/7, 9/9 and 9/30/2026. It also cites wrong Column B totals, the committee-as-payee entries and incomplete creditor names. This is the third consecutive report with a negative balance. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

FEC asks AFSCME Working Families Fund why its Form 5 shows independent expenditures but no contributions on Line 6. The October Quarterly letter says donors above $200 must be itemized, with memo text for those who gave to further independent expenditures. The fund answered the same day in a Form 99. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

FEC says Branch 193 National Association of Letter Carriers Political Action Committee's report was not signed by its listed treasurer or designated agent. The treasurer on file is Kelvin Kamachi. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)
FEC says DC Statehood PAC's multicandidate qualification date of 9/20/26 appears incorrect. The letter on Form 1M went to treasurer Allison Murray. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Harris County Democratic Party is asked why an amended June Monthly added $13,603.02 in receipts. The amended report covers 05/01/2026 - 05/31/2026 and was received 08/31/2026. The treasurer is Traci Gibson. The party filed a separate Form 99 on misdirected receipts, listed below. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Hemp Industry & Farmers of America is asked about apparent excess contributions and receipts from unregistered organizations. The May Quarterly letter notes the committee has a Non-Contribution Account under Carey v. FEC and asks it to amend if the money went there. The treasurer is Paul Kilgore. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

FEC says Invest in Tomorrow Coalition PAC may have filed late 24-hour reports on last-minute independent expenditures. The September Monthly letter (08/01/2026 - 08/31/2026) went to treasurer Brendan Bell. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Money Game Political Action Committee is asked whether receipts labeled 'Unitemized Small Contributions' include donors above $200. The letter concerns an amended April Quarterly received 07/10/2026. The treasurer is Allen Watson. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

NY Republican Federal Campaign Committee is asked about Schedule B contributions that appear to exceed the $5,000 per-election limit to a candidate. The September Monthly letter went to treasurer Steven Wells. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

FEC tells Ready for AOC its name uses a federal candidate's name without appearing to be that candidate's authorized committee. The Statement of Organization letter went to treasurer Howie Stanger. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rolling Sea Action Fund is asked why an amended April Quarterly added $16,459.12 in receipts and cut $20,000 in disbursements. The four-item letter also flags wrong Line 8 cash calculations and receipts from unregistered organizations. The amended report was received 10/15/2026. This is one of three same-day letters to treasurer Jason Hinton. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rolling Sea Action Fund is asked about Line 8 calculations and receipts from unregistered organizations on an amended July Quarterly. The amended report was received 10/15/2026. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

Rolling Sea Action Fund is told the Line 8 calculations on its amended July 2025 report appear incorrect. The amended report covers 01/01/2025 - 06/30/2025 and was received 10/15/2026. Response due 11/25. (RFAI)

The Conservative Caucus, doing business as Americans for Constitutional Liberty, is asked to fix nine independent-expenditure entries listing the wrong office sought. The October Quarterly Form 5 letter lists, for example, Sarah Trone Garriott (Iowa 3rd) disclosed under California 13th, and Abdul El-Sayed (Michigan Senate) under Minnesota Senate. Other opposed candidates named are John Elias Baldacci, Adam C. Gray, Alani Ines Bankhead, Chris Pappas, Karishma Manzur, Dan Osborn and Brian Poindexter. The six-item letter also says 48-hour reports filed 8/5, 9/6, 9/19 and 10/7 do not appear on Schedule 5-E and that some 48-hour reports appear to have been filed late. It further cites donor entries reading 'Omitted/Omitted'. Response due 11/27. (RFAI)

sections.headline: 50 Form 99s: RFAI answers, 'under $5,000' statements, terminations requests and several filings worth a second look
paragraphs: Most of the batch is routine: small committees telling the FEC they have not crossed the $5,000 reporting threshold, and committees answering RFAIs. Four Angie for Florida responses came in within an hour, and Working Americans Public Action Committee filed five identical statements. More substantive items include the DSCC's loan increase to $25,000,000, Harris County Democratic Party's $148,176 in misdirected receipts, the National Association of Realtors PAC's explanation of negative Line 21b entries, and several late-filing admissions.

items: ActBlue tells the FEC a vendor offset was really income from Diamond Assets' purchase of computer equipment at fair market value. It moved the item from Line 21b to Line 17 on its April Monthly report in response to a September 23 RFAI. (Form 99)

AFSCME Working Families Fund tells the FEC it received no 'contributions' because its receipts were per capita tax payments. It says the payments were not made to influence federal elections, so no amendment is needed. The filing refers to a November 25, 2026 letter, the response date printed on its RFAI. (Form 99)
Allegheny County Democratic Committee - Federal says $7,763.32 in unitemized receipts were individual contributions below the $200 itemization threshold. (Form 99)

Angie for Florida tells the FEC it corrected missing election designations and removed duplicate receipts that had overstated an April Quarterly decrease of $78,941.28. Treasurer David Geller says the amendment moved Line 11(a)(iii) from $195,903.35 to $116,962.07 and fixed designations for donors including Bandele Onasanya and Autumn Stokes. This is one of four same-day responses to a September 17 RFAI for the committee of Florida Senate candidate Angela Nixon. (Form 99)

Angie for Florida explains $1,250 in refunded general-election excess and a corrected $1,000 contribution on its amended July Quarterly. The refunds to Autumn Stokes were $1,000 on June 20 and $250 on June 25. Reporting Stephanie Porta's April 24 contribution at its full amount raised period receipts by $500 to $410,476.85. (Form 99)

Angie for Florida says Whitney Touchton and Stanley Twiggs each gave $7,000 split between primary and general elections. The Year-End 2025 response also corrects a $5,000 contribution previously listed under 'Rashida Tlaib Campaign' to Rooted in Community Leadership PAC. It says Touchton's extra $250 was refunded January 4, 2026. (Form 99)
Angie for Florida says it recalculated Column B on its amended 12-Day Pre-Primary report. The report covers July 1 through July 29, 2026. (Form 99)
Bishop Staten for Congress says neither the candidate nor the campaign has received funds or spent over $5,000. (Form 99)

BlueWaveAmerica blames a 'faulty assumption and miscommunication' for late reporting of a founder's loan and vendor payments. The response to an October 1 RFAI covers payments to NGP Van/EveryAction, Amazon Web Services and Google GSuite, including an annual $76,000 contract the founder paid before heart surgery. It also cites loan repayments of $2,626.22 and $150 and a third amendment for payments reported on the wrong line. This is a late disclosure of the loan and payments. (Form 99)
C Monday for Liberty says the campaign has not reached the $5,000 threshold. (Form 99)

Cinquemani for Congress files a 12-page FEC Form 3 as a miscellaneous submission showing $5,657.48 raised and $3,744.69 spent. The cover page lists a coverage period of 07/01/2026 through 09/30/2026. It lists itemized receipts, disbursements including $2,294.69 in campaign event payments to multiple vendors, and an ending cash balance of $2,012.79. The committee is that of New York Republican challenger Joseph Cinquemani. (Form 99)
Cinquemani for Congress tells the FEC no Schedule C-1, loan agreement, loan forgiveness letter or debt settlement plan applies. (Form 99)

Committee for Ellis Colvin asks the FEC to terminate the committee, saying it never raised or spent more than $5,000. The Maryland 5th District candidate says his candidacy ended with the June 2026 primary. A termination approval for the committee also appears today. (Form 99)
Committee to Elect Charlotte Magoon says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold as of the 12-Day Pre-General Report. (Form 99)

Committee to Elect Jullie Kelley submits bank-balance notes showing monthly $5 service charges and an account overdrawn to -$2.97. The notes say the candidate added $30.00 of personal funds on 8/11 and the account ended September at $17.03. (Form 99)
Deborah Ann Meidinger Hosey for US Congress says it has not met the $5,000 threshold for the 12-Day Pre-General report. (Form 99)
Donhorn4congress says it has neither spent nor raised $5,000. (Form 99)

DSCC files a loan agreement amendment raising its Amalgamated Bank credit facility from $20,000,000 to $25,000,000. The Fourth Amendment, dated July 24, 2026 with a June 30 effective date, extends maturity to June 30, 2028. The updated Schedule C-1 reports a $15,000,000 drawdown and says current and future assets are pledged as collateral. Treasurer Allison Wright says the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee's extension agreement, previously filed with the August Monthly, could not be submitted electronically. (Form 99)
Elect John Badger 2028 tells the FEC 'Nothing has changed as of right now'. The committee is that of Democratic presidential candidate John Robert Badger. (Form 99)

Emmett White files a 10-page FEC Form 3 whose figures do not agree with each other. Schedule A lists a $62,568.09 receipt from Lois Brown dated 07/15/2025 and Schedule B a $62,568.09 disbursement to Emmett Lee White on 9/22/2026, while the summary page shows $1,200.00 in operating expenditures. The cover covers 09/01 - 09/22/2026, the summary page 09/01 - 09/15 and the detailed page 09/15 - 09/22. A Schedule C-1 lists the same $62,568.09 as pledged collateral. (Form 99)

Friends of Junaid says it refunded or reattributed general-election money after the candidate lost the primary. The response to a September 15 RFAI on the April Quarterly says an amended July Quarterly reattributed or redesignated what donors confirmed. The rest and an over-limit contribution were refunded on the October Quarterly. Treasurer is Victoria Perrone, for the committee of Illinois Democrat Junaid Ahmed. (Form 99)

GOPAC Election Fund tells the FEC a database error skewed cash on hand and hid donors on two amended F3X reports. Treasurer Melodie Johnson says the M9 and M10 reports had Column A errors, and several donors had not displayed properly on Lines 11a and 17. (Form 99)

Harris County Democratic Party says 42 receipts totaling $148,176 meant for state or nonfederal activities were mistakenly deposited into its federal accounts. They include $112,051 in 36 JJR contributions, $11,000 in three AuntieUp contributions, $125 tied to Christine Weems for Judge, a $15,000 AAPI-program wire and a $10,000 Annise Parker check. The party reported them on Schedule A, Line 17, on its September Form 3X. (Form 99)

Keene Democratic Committee says it has taken in and disbursed no funds. (Form 99)

McCracken for Montana says it had not passed $5,000 as of the October Quarterly close on September 30. The committee filed both statements within minutes of each other. (Form 99)
Mel Tull for Congress says it corrected the issues on its April and July Quarterly reports and resubmitted its termination report. Treasurer is Kelsey Garnatz. (Form 99)

Monte Mitchell for US Congress asks the FEC to terminate the committee, saying he lost the primary. He says there have been no donations or expenditures since and no money is in the account. (Form 99)
Natalie Rivera for US Senate 2026 says it has neither raised nor spent $5,000. (Form 99)

National Association of Realtors Political Action Committee explains negative Line 21b entries on its 12-Day Pre-election report as transfers to Line 24 independent expenditures. The Form 99 lists advance costs of $93,700 to Meath Media Group, $21,600 to Ambrosino Muir Hansen Crounse and $73,717 to Bridge Impact LLC for expenditures not yet disseminated. It says the positive Line 24 entries support candidates including Jon Husted, Ashley Hinson, Mike Rogers, Don Davis and Ashley Moody. It also describes one item as reimbursement for solicitation costs above the one-third rule. (Form 99)

No Labels PAC reports members gave $8,005,681.11 to aligned candidates through the Democracy Engine platform in the period. The statement says No Labels used its internal-communication allowance to solicit the gifts. It lists cycle totals including $734,728.81 for Susan Collins, $710,845.38 for Bill Cassidy, $420,931.72 for Mike Lawler and $416,602.90 for Josh Gottheimer. Some entries look mistyped, such as 'Michael Lawler- 62,880.00'. (Form 99)
Ramon Mora for Congress says it has not met the $5,000 reporting threshold for the 2026 general election. (Form 99)
Riven for Senate says it has not raised more than $5,000 in the specified period. (Form 99)

SD PAC says excessive contributions on its August Monthly were data-entry errors that belonged in its non-contribution account. It adds that the apparent excess items were transfers to affiliated committees, and says it filed an amended report and statement of organization. (Form 99)

Serrano for America says it has not exceeded $5,000 including the candidate's personal funds. The statement responds to the October Quarterly late notification and covers activity through September 30 and October 14. Treasurer is Gerardo Serrano. (Form 99)

State of Loc Nation for Clement for Senate restates a $50,250,000 valuation of an intellectual-property license reported as a candidate loan. The Form 99 says the license from candidate Rev. Dr. Christina Loren Clement is limited, non-exclusive and restricted to campaign purposes, and that the committee previously reported it on Form 3, Line 13(a). The valuation is unchanged from earlier filings. (Form 99)
Texas Alliance for Life Fed PAC tells the FEC a 24-hour report filed on 10/20/26 was filed in error and was not necessary. (Form 99)

The Wisco Project PAC admits filing an untimely 48-hour notice for $1,055.78 in in-kind staff time supporting Mitchell Berman in WI-01. The in-kind time from Wisco Project, Inc. began in August, so this is a late disclosure. The amendment also cuts a Rebecca Cooke (WI-03) in-kind estimate from $60,000 to $32,209.00. (Form 99)
The Women's Cabinet says it has had no transactions across five filing periods. The hybrid PAC lists the year-end 2025 period, two 2026 quarterlies and the 9/30/2026 filings. (Form 99)
Tom Schmitz for Liberty, a newly registered committee, says it has not met the $5,000 threshold for the 12-Day Pre-General Report. (Form 99)

Turn Left PAC says a $1,499.99 independent-expenditure project was double-counted and cut July Quarterly disbursements to $166,135.40. The fix reduced them from $166,790.33 and raised June 30 cash on hand from $41,635.25 to $42,290.18. It also splits the Groundfloor Political and Switchboard costs between supporting Britta Aguirre and opposing Carol Devine Miller in West Virginia's 1st District. The response answers an October 13 RFAI. (Form 99)

Veronica C. Fernandez for US Senate says its total is $4,924.10 and still under the $5,000 cap. The statement says she received another $120.00 and spent $124.75 on literature since September 30. (Form 99)
Working Americans Public Action Committee says it has had no activity this election cycle. This is the first of five identical statements filed by the committee on 10/22. (Form 99)

You Can Push Back admits its 24-hour and 48-hour independent expenditure reports were filed late. The response to a September 16 RFAI on the July Monthly blames miscommunication between consultants and its law firm. It says the late reports were filed before the election and that its Netfile software had coded expenditures with a non-FEC category. These are late disclosures. (Form 99)

apod.title: Andromeda in Southern Spring
apod.caption: Looking toward the north from Mullion, New South Wales, Australia, the Andromeda Galaxy never gets more than a few degrees above the horizon. During the southern hemisphere spring, Andromeda is highest in the sky around midnight though.
